note: Adjudicated variants: 3 accidental (punctuation, capitalization, capital-accents, accents) and 1 orthographic, where both spellings are real words of the same recension and the edition rules which it prints. Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero further divergence.

adjudicated.ruling: Both spellings are real: genetrix is the older form, genitrix the one that spread later, and the dictionaries head both. The typical edition prints Genetrícis throughout the Canon and its seasonal variants, and witness do follows it, so the edition prints that and records the hand missal's reading here rather than silently correcting a page that is not wrong. Whitaker's Words carries only genetrix; Collatinus carries both.
No comma before the et closing the list of the twelve, with do and with the typical edition, and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.suscipe-sancta-trinitas w037.
Colon closing the list of martyrs before the general et ómnium Sanctórum, with do and with the typical edition: the colon separates the named from the unnamed.
No comma before the apposition Dóminum nostrum, with handmissal-eo and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.aufer-a-nobis w018 for the same closing formula.
